external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member using the library app on a phone to borrow, renew or reserve books.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who manually extend loans, clear account blocks and mark books returned.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: Everyone at the desk uses the same shared login; individual staff members and branches cannot be identified from the history.

processes.name: library app
processes.description: The app on a member's phone through which members request borrowing, renewals and reservations.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The REST API that checks loan rules and reads or writes loan records; it is the only stated interface for touching loans.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: Authentication is not established. Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in" and could not say what it accepts or does with rejected calls. Exposure is disputed: Lending service note says "The lending API is internal-only"; Interview transcript says "The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet."

processes.name: self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where members scan their library card and books being borrowed or returned.
processes.source_excerpt: Every branch has self-service kiosks where a member scans their library card and the books they are borrowing or returning.
processes.notes: The kiosk's direct interaction with the loans database is unknown; only data arriving at the lending API was observed.

processes.name: circulation page
processes.description: The page used by desk staff to manually change loan and member account records.
processes.source_excerpt: someone at the desk opens the circulation page and marks it returned, or clears the block on the account.
processes.notes: The page uses one shared desk login and does not ask again for the user's identity.

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: The single database containing members, loans, reservations, contact details and borrowing histories.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: The earlier statement about two databases was corrected in the same source: "We merged those in the spring. It's one loans database now. The old reservations database is gone."

data_flows.name: request loan action
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to request a borrow, renewal or reservation.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
data_flows.data_description: Member and book details for borrowing, renewing or reserving a title.

data_flows.name: change loan
data_flows.description: The library app sends a loan renewal, borrowing request or reservation request to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member, and the API checks the loan rules and writes the change.
data_flows.notes: The API's authentication check is unknown; Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in" and would have to look.
data_flows.data_description: The selected book or title and member identity, for a loan change or reservation.

data_flows.name: send loan return
data_flows.description: A kiosk sends scanned loan and return transactions to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API.
data_flows.data_description: Member card, book and loan or return transaction details.

data_flows.name: manage loan
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page to extend loans, clear account blocks or mark books returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand, through a circulation page the lending API serves.
data_flows.notes: All desk staff use the same shared login.
data_flows.data_description: Member account and loan changes made by desk staff.

data_flows.name: change loan
data_flows.description: The circulation page submits manual loan and account changes to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: someone at the desk opens the circulation page and marks it returned, or clears the block on the account.
data_flows.notes: The page is served by the lending API. The shared account prevents attribution to an individual staff member or branch.
data_flows.data_description: Manual loan-return, loan-extension and account-block changes.

data_flows.name: read-write loans
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: Member records, loans, reservations and borrowing histories.

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network on which branch kiosks and desk staff operate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data-centre zone where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

trust_boundaries.name: member phones
trust_boundaries.description: The member-controlled phone environment hosting the library app.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database is confidential because it contains names, email addresses, home addresses and members' full borrowing histories.
assumptions.basis: Interview transcript explicitly states that these personal details and borrowing histories live in the loans database.
